1970 Dodge Challenger R/T SE Hemi Tribute Was Parked in 1987, Restored for MCACN 2026
9 photos
Photo: Geoff Stunkard's Zookeeper's Diary/YouTube
Introduced in 1970, the Dodge Challenger spent only two years on the muscle car market. But that was enough to establish it as one of America's most iconic vehicles from the era. Over 50 years later, the Challenger is a highly desirable classic.
Of course, some old-school Challengers are more sought-after than others. While the base model doesn't get a lot of attention, the R/T version stands out at public auctions. Add a Hemi into the mix, and collectors will throw six-figure sums at it.
The range-topping option in 1970, the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi is quite rare. Dodge built only 356 units with this powerplant, which is less than 0.5% of all the Challengers built in 1970 (76,935 examples).
It's unclear exactly how many of these Mopars are still around today, but the Hemi Challenger R/T is so desirable that many enthusiasts have built tribute cars. Most aren't all that great, but some are so accurate that you can barely set them apart from the real deal. This green R/T SE that was recently unveiled at the 2026 Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals (MCACN) is one of them.
This Challenger was born as a true R/T SE. The SE stands for Special Edition, which was a luxury and styling trim option. It was available on both the standard and R/T models and included a vinyl top with a smaller "formal" rear window. It also had SE medallions on the C-pillars, leather/vinyl bucket seats, an overhead console, and upscale trim accents.
Records show that Dodge sold 9,976 cars with the SE package, including 3,753 R/T models. Because it was born with a 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8, which was standard on the R/T, this Challenger is one of 2,522 units made. It was already a pretty rare car when it rolled off the assembly line.
How did it end up with a Hemi? Well, it's not a recent build with a crate engine . This Mopar flaunts a true 426 Hemi. The powerplant found its way into the car in 1981, when the current owner bought it with an empty engine bay. He got a used Hemi V8 and immediately planted it under the hood. Six years later, however, he put the Challenger into storage.
Nearly four decades later, he decided that the Mopar deserved a second chance, and he took it to Apex Automotive. The vehicle was restored to factory specifications, but the 426 Hemi engine was retained. Moreover, the engine bay was detailed to look like this Challenger was actually born with a Hemi.
Had it been a true Hemi Challenger R/T SE, this hardtop would have been one of only 60 units produced. That's the type of production number that comes with a six-figure value exceeding $200,000 in this type of condition. It's obviously not the case here, but this Challenger has to be one of the finest Hemi tribute cars out there.
What's your take on replicas ? Do you think these cars can shine next to the real deal? Check out this Challenger in the video below and let me know in the comments section.
